portName: Passenger Terminal Amsterdam (PTA), with overflow calls at IJmuiden
townName: the canal ring and Centraal Station area
seoTitle: Amsterdam cruise port guide: PTA, IJmuiden and museums
seoDescription: Amsterdam cruise port 2026: PTA is a 15 min walk to Centraal. GVB day ticket from €10, Rijksmuseum €25, Anne Frank €16.50 online only, €15 cruise tax.
quickAnswer: Most sea cruise ships dock at Passenger Terminal Amsterdam (PTA) on Piet Heinkade, a flat 15-minute walk east of Centraal Station; tram 26 also runs to Centraal. Some ships use the Felison Cruise Terminal in IJmuiden instead, about 30–35 km away, which needs a shuttle, bus plus train, or taxi. From PTA, leave Museumplein by 15:30 or Centraal by 16:00 for a 17:30 all-aboard.
intro: Amsterdam is one of the few big European cities where a sea cruise ship ties up within walking distance of the old centre. That is changing. From 2026 the city allows one sea cruise ship a day at PTA and no more than 100 sea cruise calls a year, so more ships are being moved to IJmuiden on the North Sea coast, about an hour from the centre by public transport. Check your berth before planning. The city's three big museums all run on timed tickets, and the Anne Frank House is sold online only and sells out weeks ahead, so book before you sail. Amsterdam also charges cruise passengers a day-tourist tax of €15 per person (2026), billed through the ship.

terminals.name: Passenger Terminal Amsterdam (PTA), Piet Heinkade 27
terminals.notes: The city-centre terminal on the IJ, east of Centraal Station, with a 600 m quay for ships up to about 340 m. From 2026 only one sea cruise ship a day can berth here. Exit the building, turn right (west) and follow Piet Heinkade to Centraal in 10–15 minutes. Tram 26 stops at Muziekgebouw, a few minutes' walk away, and runs to Centraal. Taxis wait outside. Luggage lockers in the terminal take coins only.

terminals.name: Felison Cruise Terminal, IJmuiden (Cruiseboulevard 10)
terminals.notes: On the North Sea coast at the mouth of the North Sea Canal, about 30–35 km from the centre. Used by large ships and by calls that cannot get a PTA slot. Many lines run a paid shuttle coach to central Amsterdam. Public transport is Connexxion bus 382 from the IJmuiden Badweg stop on the road outside to Amsterdam Sloterdijk, then a short train to Centraal. Taxis take about 30 minutes without traffic.

terminals.name: Coenhaven
terminals.notes: Industrial port area west of the centre where some ships have berthed. Not walkable to the old town; rely on the ship's shuttle or a taxi.

walkability.detail: From PTA the walk to Centraal Station is flat and about 10–15 minutes along Piet Heinkade and the IJ waterfront. From Centraal, Dam Square is about 10 minutes south along the Damrak, and the Anne Frank House about 20 minutes west. The Rijksmuseum and Van Gogh Museum are further, best reached by tram. Watch for cycle paths: they look like pavements, bikes come fast and have priority. From IJmuiden, nothing is walkable.

transportSections.detail: Turn right out of the terminal and follow the waterfront west. Flat and paved all the way. Stay off the red cycle lanes.

transportSections.cost: €3.40 one-hour ticket bought on board by card (2026), or tap in with a bank card
transportSections.detail: Muziekgebouw Bimhuis stop is about 4 minutes' walk from PTA. Useful if you have mobility problems; otherwise walking is about as quick. Trams and buses do not take cash.

transportSections.cost: Bank-card tap: €1.16 boarding fee plus a distance charge, capped at €10.50 a day (GVB Max); GVB day tickets from €10 (2026)
transportSections.time: Allow 35–45 min door to door from PTA to the Rijksmuseum
transportSections.detail: From Centraal take tram 2 or 12 to the Rijksmuseum stop. For the Van Gogh Museum use the Van Baerlestraat or Museumplein stops. Pay by tapping a contactless bank card or phone on the reader when you get on and again when you get off (OVpay). Each person needs their own card or phone. Forgetting to tap out leaves you charged a higher fare.

Covers GVB trams, buses and metro. Buy in the GVB app or by card on board. Only worth it if you will take three or more rides; a typical cruise day with a return tram trip to Museumplein costs less on bank-card tap with the €10.50 daily cap as a safety net.

transportSections.cost: Varies by line; check your cruise planner
transportSections.time: About 30–45 min each way plus loading
transportSections.detail: The simplest option from IJmuiden. Check the drop-off point and the last return time in your daily programme.

transportSections.cost: Pay by contactless bank card on the bus, then a train fare from Sloterdijk
transportSections.time: About 45 min by bus to Sloterdijk, about 1 hour to Centraal in total
transportSections.detail: Board at IJmuiden Badweg, on the road outside the terminal. The bus runs about every 15 minutes to Amsterdam Sloterdijk, where frequent trains run to Centraal. Tap in and out with the same bank card on both bus and train.

transportSections.cost: Metered; from IJmuiden about €80–125 each way
transportSections.time: About 30 min from IJmuiden without traffic; a few minutes from PTA
transportSections.detail: Taxis wait at PTA. From IJmuiden a taxi is the fastest way back if you are running late, but it is expensive. Agree on the meter, not a fixed price, with street taxis.

returnTiming.rule: For a 17:30 all-aboard at PTA: leave Museumplein by 15:30 and Centraal by 16:00. At IJmuiden by bus and train: be at Centraal by 14:45; by ship shuttle, follow the last shuttle time.
returnTiming.detail: Tram from the Rijksmuseum to Centraal plus the 15-minute walk to PTA takes 35–45 minutes, and trams slow down in the afternoon. That gets you on board 60 minutes before all-aboard. From IJmuiden the public transport return is about an hour with a change at Sloterdijk, so treat it as a train-dependent trip and aim to be on board 90 minutes early.
returnTiming.emergencyFallback: From the centre, a taxi to PTA takes a few minutes. From the centre to IJmuiden, a taxi takes about 30 minutes outside rush hour and costs about €80–125. Call the port agent number in your daily programme if you will be late.

excursionAdvice: From PTA, Amsterdam is easy to do alone: the centre is a walk away, trams take bank cards, and the museums sell timed tickets online. A ship tour is worth it in three cases: when your ship berths at IJmuiden and you want a guaranteed ride back, when you want to see the countryside (Zaanse Schans windmills, Volendam, Keukenhof in spring) without working out regional buses, and when you missed the Anne Frank House release, because ship tours sometimes hold group slots. Check what the tour includes; a 'canal cruise and city tour' you can do yourself for much less from the piers outside Centraal.

dayPlan.intro: Assumes docking at PTA at 08:00, a Rijksmuseum slot at 09:00 and an Anne Frank House slot at about 13:30, both booked online before the cruise.

steps.what: Walk west from PTA along the IJ to Centraal Station (about 15 minutes).
Tram 2 or 12 from Centraal to the Rijksmuseum stop. Tap in and out with a contactless bank card.
Rijksmuseum at opening. Two hours covers the Gallery of Honour and The Night Watch.
Walk north through the canal ring (Spiegelgracht, the Nine Streets) towards the Jordaan, about 30 minutes at an easy pace.
Lunch in the Jordaan or the Nine Streets.
Anne Frank House at your booked time; allow about an hour. Bags bigger than A4 are not allowed.
Walk to Dam Square (about 10 minutes) and down the Damrak to Centraal. If time allows, take a canal cruise from the piers opposite the station, but only one that is back by 16:00.
Leave Centraal and walk 15 minutes east to PTA.
Back on board, 60 minutes before all-aboard.

sights.name: Rijksmuseum
sights.why: The national museum: Rembrandt's The Night Watch, Vermeer and the Dutch Golden Age collection.
sights.tip: Open daily 09:00–17:00. Everyone, including children, needs a timed slot booked online; tickets are not sold at the door.

sights.name: Van Gogh Museum
sights.why: The largest Van Gogh collection in the world, across Museumplein from the Rijksmuseum.
sights.cost: Charged, under-18s free; check the museum's own site for the 2026 adult price
sights.tip: Online timed tickets only. Usually open to 18:00, later on most Fridays. Doing both this and the Rijksmuseum in one cruise day is tiring; pick one.

sights.name: Anne Frank House
sights.why: The canal house on the Prinsengracht where Anne Frank's family hid, including the Secret Annex.
sights.tip: Online only, never at the door. Tickets go on sale every Tuesday at 10:00 Amsterdam time for visits six weeks later and sell out within hours; a smaller batch for the following week is released at the same time. No waiting list.

sights.name: Canal ring (Grachtengordel) and the Nine Streets
sights.why: The 17th-century canals of Herengracht, Keizersgracht and Prinsengracht, with small shops in the Nine Streets that cross them.
sights.tip: Walk it between the Rijksmuseum and the Anne Frank House instead of taking the tram.

sights.name: Canal cruise
sights.why: The easiest way to see the canal houses and bridges without walking, and dry on a wet day.
sights.cost: Varies by operator; check before boarding
sights.tip: Several operators sail from the piers opposite Centraal, close to PTA. Check the return time before you buy.

sights.name: Dam Square and the Royal Palace
sights.why: The city's main square, ten minutes from Centraal, with the former town hall that is now a royal palace.
sights.cost: Square free; palace charged when open
sights.tip: The Damrak between Centraal and Dam is crowded and full of tourist shops; take the parallel streets for a quieter walk.

sights.name: Jordaan
sights.why: Former working-class district west of the canal ring, now cafés, galleries and courtyard almshouses (hofjes).
sights.tip: Combine with the Anne Frank House, which is on its edge. The Noordermarkt has a market on Mondays and Saturdays.

sights.name: Zaanse Schans (on a long call)
sights.why: Working windmills and wooden houses on the Zaan river north-west of the city.
sights.tip: Easiest as a ship tour. If you go alone, check entry rules on the site before you go.

beaches.name: Zandvoort aan Zee
beaches.howToGetThere: Train from Amsterdam Centraal (direct or via Haarlem).
beaches.note: Amsterdam has no swimming beach in the centre. Only worth it if you skip the city. From IJmuiden, the IJmuiden beach is closer to the terminal than Amsterdam is.

commonMistakes.mistake: Planning to buy Anne Frank House tickets on the day.
commonMistakes.fix: They are sold online only, released on Tuesdays at 10:00 for six weeks ahead. Set a reminder as soon as you know your port date.

commonMistakes.mistake: Turning up at the Rijksmuseum or Van Gogh Museum without a timed ticket.
commonMistakes.fix: Book a slot online before you sail. Neither sells tickets at the door.

commonMistakes.mistake: Assuming the ship docks in central Amsterdam.
commonMistakes.fix: With the 2026 limit of one ship a day at PTA, many calls go to IJmuiden, about an hour away. Check the berth in your cruise documents.

commonMistakes.mistake: Walking in the red cycle lanes.
commonMistakes.fix: They look like pavements but bikes and mopeds come fast and have priority. Look both ways before stepping off the kerb.

commonMistakes.mistake: Trying to pay for the tram with cash, or forgetting to tap out.
commonMistakes.fix: Trams and buses take cards only. Tap your bank card or phone on the reader getting on and getting off; each traveller needs their own card.

commonMistakes.mistake: Hanging a bag on a café chair.
commonMistakes.fix: Keep it on your lap or between your feet. Bag thieves work the restaurants and cafés of the centre.

safety: Amsterdam is safe for day visitors, but pickpocketing and bag theft are common in the centre, especially around Centraal Station and on trains and trams to and from Centraal and Schiphol. Thieves often work in pairs, with one creating a distraction. In restaurants, thieves posing as sellers or as someone looking for a friend walk in and take bags from chairs. The bigger everyday risk is traffic: cyclists and mopeds move fast, often ignore red lights, and have priority on cycle paths. Do not swim in the canals; it is dangerous and fined. Avoid quiet alleys in the Red Light District late at night and do not engage with anyone offering drugs.
scams: Fake police: people posing as plain-clothes officers ask to inspect your cash or bank cards for counterfeits and take them. Dutch police rarely do this; refuse and call the police information line 0900 8844 if in doubt.
Distraction theft in restaurants: someone comes in selling something or asking about a friend while an accomplice lifts a bag from a chair back. Keep bags on your lap.
Pickpocket pairs on trams and trains around Centraal: one person blocks or bumps you while the other takes a phone or wallet. Keep valuables in front pockets or a zipped bag.
accessibility: PTA is a modern terminal, and the walk to Centraal is flat and paved; tram 26 is an alternative for the first stretch. Check step-free access with each museum when booking. The historic centre has narrow pavements, bridges with slopes, and parked bikes everywhere. Canal houses, including the Anne Frank House's Secret Annex, have very steep stairs. Canal cruise boats vary in access, so ask before buying. From IJmuiden, the cruise line shuttle is the practical choice for wheelchair users.
rainyDay: Amsterdam handles rain well. The Rijksmuseum and Van Gogh Museum fill a day on their own, and a covered canal cruise from the piers opposite Centraal is a dry way to see the canals. NEMO science museum is a short walk from PTA. Book museum slots in advance, because rainy days fill them quickly.
crowdTips: The Damrak, Dam Square and the Red Light District are crowded all day. The Rijksmuseum is quietest at the 09:00 opening; the Anne Frank House is sold out weeks ahead, so the queue you see is for people with tickets. From 2026 the city allows one sea cruise ship a day at PTA and no more than 100 sea cruise calls a year, down from about 190, and requires shore power from 2027. In January 2026 the city executive backed ending sea cruise calls in Amsterdam by 2035; the final decision was left to the council elected in March 2026. Amsterdam charges a day-tourist tax of €15 per person per day (2026) on cruise passengers aged 2 and over, declared by the ship and normally passed on in your fare or port charges.

faqs.q: Is Amsterdam cruise port walkable to the city centre?
faqs.a: Yes, from Passenger Terminal Amsterdam. Centraal Station is a flat 10–15 minute walk west along the waterfront, and Dam Square is 10 minutes further. If your ship docks at IJmuiden, it is not walkable: the centre is 30–35 km away.
No. Ships dock alongside at PTA in the city or at the Felison Cruise Terminal in IJmuiden.

faqs.q: How do I get from IJmuiden cruise terminal to Amsterdam?
faqs.a: Take your cruise line's shuttle (30–45 minutes), or Connexxion bus 382 from IJmuiden Badweg to Amsterdam Sloterdijk (about 45 minutes) and a train to Centraal, about an hour in total, paying by contactless bank card. A taxi takes about 30 minutes and costs about €80–125.

faqs.q: How do I get from the cruise terminal to the Rijksmuseum?
faqs.a: Walk 15 minutes to Centraal, then take tram 2 or 12 to the Rijksmuseum stop. Allow 35–45 minutes door to door. Pay by tapping a contactless bank card or phone.

faqs.q: Can I get Anne Frank House tickets on the day?
faqs.a: Usually not. Tickets are sold online only, released every Tuesday at 10:00 Amsterdam time for visits six weeks later, and they sell out within hours. The adult price is €16.50 (2026).

faqs.q: Do cruise passengers pay Amsterdam's tourist tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Amsterdam charges a day-tourist tax of €15 per person per day (2026) on cruise passengers aged 2 and over. The ship declares it, so you do not pay it in town.

faqs.q: What can I do in Amsterdam in one day from a cruise ship?
faqs.a: From PTA: the Rijksmuseum at opening, a walk through the canal ring and the Jordaan, the Anne Frank House with a pre-booked slot, and a canal cruise from outside Centraal before walking back.

faqs.q: Is Amsterdam safe for cruise passengers?
faqs.a: Yes, with care. Watch for pickpockets around Centraal and on trams, keep bags off chair backs, ignore anyone claiming to be plain-clothes police who wants to see your cash, and stay out of the cycle lanes.
